title: Meet Quadric on the Road: Three Must-Attend AI Events - Semiwiki
gist: Quadric is using three August-September 2026 industry events to promote its Chimera GPNPU, a fully programmable, unified processor architecture pitched as an alternative to fixed-function NPUs for on-device and physical AI workloads.

insights.claim: Quadric's Chimera general-purpose neural processing unit (GPNPU) merges AI graph execution and conventional C++ processing into a single code stream, unlike fixed-function NPUs that require workloads to be partitioned across accelerator, CPU, and DSP resources.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A unified programmable architecture could differentiate Quadric versus fixed-function edge AI accelerator competitors as on-device AI workloads evolve faster than silicon refresh cycles.
insights.quote: Chimera is designed to merge AI graph execution and conventional C++ processing into a single code stream.
insights.locator: Across all three events, the common theme is control

insights.claim: Quadric's Chimera SDK supports importing trained ONNX models and quantizing, compiling, simulating, validating, and profiling them before hardware is available, aiming to simplify integration for SoC customers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pre-silicon software tooling maturity is a competitive factor in IP licensing decisions for SoC design teams evaluating NPU IP vendors.
insights.quote: The Chimera SDK supports importing trained ONNX models, quantizing, compiling, simulating, validating, and profiling them before hardware is required.
insights.locator: The Chimera SDK supports importing trained ONNX models

insights.claim: Quadric argues that AI models are advancing faster than fixed-function accelerators can accommodate, positioning fully programmable processors as necessary so device makers can adapt to new operators and workloads without redesigning silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A structural argument for programmable NPU IP over fixed-function accelerator IP in edge and embedded AI licensing markets.
insights.quote: Models are advancing faster than conventional fixed-function accelerators can comfortably accommodate
insights.locator: The session arrives at a critical moment

insights.claim: Quadric CTO and cofounder Nigel Drego will present 'Take Control: A Processor Designed for On-Device AI' at the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 16, 2026, reflecting the company's push from cloud-only AI toward on-device inference.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An event-calendar marker for tracking Quadric's on-device AI positioning versus rivals at major industry gatherings.
insights.locator: Next, Quadric heads to the AI Infra Summit

insights.claim: Quadric will present on porting vision-language-action (VLA) models to embedded NPUs at Embedded World North America on September 24, 2026, targeting robotics, autonomous machines, and automotive physical AI applications.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Indicates Quadric is chasing the physical AI and robotics edge-inference opportunity, a growth vector beyond typical mobile and IoT edge AI.
insights.locator: Quadric's third stop is Embedded World North America
